body:
Spec: docs/specs/issue-autopilot-local.md, section 14 'Required changes outside packages/autopilot'. This ticket is the PREREQUISITE of the @adlc/autopilot build ticket: every flag below is consumed by the autopilot orchestrator and none of them changes fleet's default behaviour when absent. Fleet is NOT trust-root tier, but env-scrub.mjs and sandbox.mjs are railed here because the autopilot's threat model (spec section 11) rests on them being unchanged.

=== TASK ===
Add to packages/fleet (bin/fleet.mjs + lib/config.mjs + lib/run.mjs + lib/scheduler.mjs + lib/charters.mjs + lib/review-runner.mjs) the following OPERATOR-LOCAL CLI flags and config keys. Operator-local means: honoured from argv only; if the same key appears in the repo-committed .adlc/config.json fleet block it is warned and ignored, exactly as fleet.adapter / fleet.model are today (lib/config.mjs N1/K1 pattern).

1. --no-pr : skip openPR at run end; the integration branch is left for the caller. Default unchanged (fleet opens exactly one PR).
2. --no-complete : skip completeTicketOnIntegration after the post-merge gate; the caller owns ticket completion. Default unchanged.
3. --dead-end-file <path> : the file's content (fenced by charters.fence, DEAD_END_MAX_CHARS cap) becomes the initial dead-end material for strike 1, so a caller can hand fleet the previous round's failure (preflight log, CI job log, conflict markers). Default: no initial dead-ends.
4. --max-strikes <n> : replaces the hard-coded maxStrikes = 2 in advanceTicket. Integer 1..50. Default 2.
5. --wall-clock-minutes <m> : an external deadline for the WHOLE run; when it expires fleet stops dispatching, records reason 'wall-clock', exits 2, and leaves the run resumable. Default: none (existing per-dispatch timeoutMinutes still applies).
6. --charter-file <path> : the file's content is appended to builderPrompt AFTER the Constraints block (so the Constraints stay authoritative). Default: none.
7. --pre-strike-argv <json-array> and --pre-strike-env <json-object> : a JSON array of strings executed with execFile-style argv and NO shell before every strike, with EXACTLY the environment given in --pre-strike-env (fleet adds nothing from its own env or the worker's; ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY in the object is rejected with exit 1), argv[0] required to be an absolute path. Non-zero exit → fleet stops cleanly with reason 'quota-paused', exit 2, run resumable through the EXISTING status reconciliation (lib/resume.mjs reconcileRun) on the next identical invocation — fleet has no --resume flag and this ticket adds none. Default: none.
8. fleet.reviewMaxBytes (repo config key, default 262144) forwarded to review-runner as adversarial-review --max-bytes; --allow-summary-review is never passed.
9. --json result document gains: fleetRunId; review: { provider, verdict, revision, rounds }; and a machine-readable top-level reason from the fixed set { quota-paused, lock-held, wall-clock, strikes-exhausted, ticket-blocked, flail, review-unavailable, mirror-fetch-failed } for every non-zero exit. The numeric exit code is unchanged; reason is authoritative for callers.
11. --model-plane-read host|bounded and --model-plane-read-only <abs,abs,...> (operator-local): 'bounded' selects lib/sandbox.mjs READ_POLICY.BOUNDED for the MODEL plane (worktree + the adapter's synthetic home per homeState + the allowlist) instead of READ_POLICY.HOST; default unchanged ('host'). In bounded mode fleet additionally mounts a private empty tmpfs at /tmp (bwrap --tmpfs /tmp) and sets TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP to a directory inside it, so the host /tmp is neither readable nor writable; every --model-plane-read-only entry is bound as given (a FILE entry is bound as a single read-only file, a directory as a directory) so callers can bind individual executables. The --json result reports the effective readPolicy and privateTmp:true so a caller can assert them.
12. --model-plane-git mirror --model-plane-git-mirror <abs bare repo> (operator-local, requires --model-plane-read bounded): the worker's nested worktree is cut from the caller-supplied bare mirror (git -C <mirror> worktree add ... or a clone of it) instead of from the shared repository; the mirror is a WRITABLE root for the worker (commits write objects, refs and worktree metadata into it) and, together with the worker's own worktree, is excluded from the read-only bind list; <repo>/.git is never bound; after the worker exits, fleet synchronizes the worker branch back with an explicit sequence: git -C <repo> fetch <mirror> +refs/heads/<workerBranch>:refs/fleet/fetched/<workerBranch> (temporary ref), git merge-base --is-ancestor <cutTip> refs/fleet/fetched/<workerBranch>, then git update-ref refs/heads/<workerBranch> refs/fleet/fetched/<workerBranch> <cutTip> (compare-and-swap; the worker branch is never checked out in <repo>), then delete the temporary ref — so that the worker branch then exists in <repo> (the caller repository) where the integration worktree and fleet/run-<id> are built — gates, prosecution and the merge into fleet/run-<id> then operate on that fetched-back branch exactly as in shared mode; any step failing → exit 2 reason 'mirror-fetch-failed' with the branch ref untouched. The caller owns creating the mirror (only objects reachable from the pinned base and the issue branch; no remotes, hooks or extra config). --json reports gitSource:'mirror' and the mirror path. Default unchanged (shared repository).
10. fleet run invoked with cwd = a LINKED git worktree must read that worktree's .adlc/tickets/ (not the main worktree's) and must create its nested worktrees under <cwd>/.worktrees/ and its integration worktree at <cwd>/.worktrees/fleet-integration. Verify, do not assume: today's worktrees.mjs resolves paths relative to repo root discovery.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
AC1. Every flag above has a captured-argv or captured-config unit test in packages/fleet/test/ proving (a) the documented effect and (b) that omitting the flag leaves existing behaviour byte-identical (existing fleet tests still pass unchanged). VERIFY: node --test packages/fleet/test/ exit code 0.
AC2. Operator-local enforcement: a repo .adlc/config.json fleet block that sets maxStrikes, wallClockMinutes, charterFile, preStrikeArgv, noPr, noComplete or deadEndFile produces the SECURITY warning and is ignored. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/config.test.mjs asserts the warning text and the resolved value for each key.
AC3. --pre-strike-argv is executed with shell:false and an argv array; a value containing shell metacharacters ('--model', 'opus;touch /tmp/x') reaches the child as ONE argv element and spawns no extra process. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/pre-strike.test.mjs with a spawn recorder asserting argv and shell:false; ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY absent from the child env.
AC4. --pre-strike-argv non-zero exit stops the run with reason 'quota-paused', exit 2, status file persisted, and a second identical fleet run invocation resumes via reconcileRun (stderr 'resuming run <id>', same fleetRunId in --json) from the same strike count; no --resume flag exists. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/scheduler.test.mjs + resume.test.mjs.
AC5. --wall-clock-minutes expiry mid-strike kills the worker process group, records reason 'wall-clock', exits 2. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/run.test.mjs with fake timers.
AC6. --json carries fleetRunId, review.{provider,verdict,revision,rounds} and reason for each non-zero path in the reason set; an exit-2 path with no reason is a test failure. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/json-result.test.mjs table-driven over the reason set.
AC7. --charter-file content appears in the builder prompt AFTER the Constraints block and the Constraints text is unchanged. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/charters.test.mjs asserts ordering by index.
AC8. Linked-worktree invocation: a test creates a real temporary repo, adds a linked worktree containing an extra ticket shard, runs fleet run --dry-run --json from inside it, and asserts the plan lists that shard and the planned worktree paths are under the linked worktree. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/linked-worktree.test.mjs exit code 0.
AC12. --model-plane-read bounded makes the sandbox args for the MODEL plane use READ_POLICY.BOUNDED with the given allowlist (assert no '--ro-bind / /' and that each allowlist path appears as an --ro-bind), the worker cannot read a file outside the set, a pre-existing host /tmp file is absent inside the sandbox and a write to /tmp lands in the private tmpfs, a single-file read-only entry exposes only that file and not its siblings (real bwrap test, skipped loudly without bwrap), and --json reports readPolicy 'bounded' and privateTmp true; omitting the flag keeps today's host policy byte-identical. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/model-plane-read.test.mjs exit code 0.
AC13. --model-plane-git mirror: a real-bwrap test (skipped loudly without bwrap) in which the worker process runs git rev-parse HEAD and git log successfully inside its worktree, cannot read <repo>/.git at all (ENOENT/EACCES), and git for-each-ref inside the worker lists only the issue branch; after the worker commits, fleet's fetch-back places the commit on <repo>'s worker branch; a non-fast-forward fetch → exit 2 reason mirror-fetch-failed; --json reports gitSource mirror; omitting the flag keeps today's behaviour byte-identical. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs exit code 0.
AC9. reviewMaxBytes reaches adversarial-review as --max-bytes <n>; --allow-summary-review never appears. VERIFY: packages/fleet/test/review-runner.test.mjs argv assertion.
AC10. Rails: packages/fleet/lib/env-scrub.mjs and sandbox.mjs are unchanged (protected-paths.mjs is not railed so open issue #632 can be fixed independently). VERIFY: adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this id> exit code 0.
AC11. README + toolkit page document every new flag and the reason set; the dispatcher guard passes. VERIFY: node --test apps/docs/test/*.test.mjs exit code 0.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===
Destination-allowlisting egress proxy inside the model plane's network namespace (v2 of the K2 boundary; today the model plane has unfiltered egress by design). The autopilot package itself, .adlc/config.json, any change to fleet's sandbox/env-scrub/protected-path logic, PR body content.
title: Fleet extensions the issue autopilot composes over (spec issue-autopilot-local §14)
